name: Akkub
overview: Akkub was a male Levite who served as one of the gatekeepers, a role of responsibility in the service of the temple as recorded in 1 Chronicles, Ezra, and Nehemiah. His position highlights his role in maintaining the sanctity and order of the temple precincts. There are no additional notes recorded about him beyond this significant duty.
namesAndTitles: The name Akkub means 'guard,' which aptly reflects his role as a gatekeeper in the temple. This proper name, found in 1 Chronicles 9:17, emphasizes his function in guarding and overseeing the temple entrances.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly identifies Akkub as a descendant of Korah, linking him to a notable Levitical family line as stated in 1 Chronicles 9:19. Beyond this, no other family relationships are recorded for Akkub.
scriptureSignificance: Akkub's significance lies in his service as a gatekeeper, a vital role entrusted to the Levites to protect the holiness of God's house. His Levitical heritage and connection to Korah underscore the continuity of temple service within specific families. By fulfilling this duty, Akkub contributed to the orderly worship and reverence of God’s presence among His people.
